findings_WRITTEN.Q_shape: In the |Sigma|=4 strata, the Walsh transform of 1_Q is 8[a=0] - sum_i g_i c_(a+a_i), and the product of the four signs is -(-1)^Bbar(v1,v2). For alpha=4, Q is an affine 2-flat. For alpha=6, Q is a zero-sum 6-set with A_4 = 0 that lies in no affine 3-flat; its relation shape is (3,3) or (1,5).
findings_WRITTEN.R_side: For alpha=4: the odd-weight a_0 case would need c >= 10, so a_0 is +/- a character on Q and r is nonzero exactly on one coset K of Q_lin^0. For alpha=6: product over Q of a_0 = -1, r is in {0, +/-4} with six nonzero cosets N, and #(N cap A1) <= 3. Proved by the exact 6-variable census n_0 = 5 + A_4 - 5 eps_Q and n_6 = (1 + A_4 + eps_Q)/2. A hand instance (Sigma = <e_a1, e_b1>) passes every test, so neither stratum is excluded.
findings_WRITTEN.Lemma_S: If all small values lie in the cosets of a subset of an affine 2-flat, then L + 4N_+ = 0 mod 8. Consequently, in the |Sigma|=4 strata with L=12, some off-Sigma coset carries at least 2 small values, with lambda = mu mod 3. Only the stratum (alpha, L, u) = (4, 16, 8) can have all small values inside Sigma.
findings_WRITTEN.Lemma_U: For every slice, all 16 coset twisted sums upsilon_eta(a) and omega_eta(a) share one parity. A pure coset with k=8 forces alpha even and m_eta = c.eta mod 2, where c is a cubic-ANF vector shared by all such cosets; this is proved by the mod-4 weight formula.
